webui.description: Browser UI served by `nanopi webui` (packages/webui, copied to dist/webui and embedded in single-file builds)

export-html.description: HTML export templates and vendored assets (dist/core/export-html). Also the print source of a PDF: the README tells users to open the exported HTML in a browser and print it

export-markdown.description: Session export to Markdown (the /export command, --export-format md, and the RPC export_session command). Dropping it leaves the HTML export, which renders in the browser from the template's own data payload

docs.description: In-package documentation (embedded in single-file builds; the npm package always ships it)

examples.description: In-package examples (embedded in single-file builds; the npm package always ships them)

tools.description: Built-in tool set the build registers, as a group key over the per-tool components: every "tools/<name>" was a switch in older configs and is derived from the flavor's tool set instead

tools/read.description: The read tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/bash.description: The bash tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/powershell.description: The powershell tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/edit.description: The edit tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/write.description: The write tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/grep.description: The grep tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/find.description: The find tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

tools/ls.description: The ls tool definition; a flavor whose tool set lists its tools keeps only the listed ones (see scripts/build-tools.mjs)

embedded-code.description: Embedded-code detection for shell call display (heredoc bodies and interpreter inline scripts); dropping it renders shell commands as one block

jiti-modules.description: Loading module files from disk with jiti: .nanopi/extensions/, the agent directory's extensions/, and $NANOPI_EXTENSIONS. Dropping it takes jiti out of the build, which leaves only the compiled-in modules (the single-file build never loads disk modules either way)

syntax-highlight.description: highlight.js grammars and the code highlighting the TUI uses; dropping it renders code blocks in the plain output color and takes ~1.4 MiB of grammars out of the bundle

goal.description: Goal tracking module (planned; registered so its build wiring lands with the module)

toolset.description: Built-in tool set the build registers: "standard" (read, bash, edit, write plus the optional tools) or "bash" (the shell tools alone). Flavors set it as a name, not a switch; group keys like "module/*" work here too

providers.description: Provider set the build registers: one entry from the top-level "providerSets" map. The build's model catalogs are generated for that set only, so a trimmed build carries no code or data for the providers it drops. Flavors set it as a name, not a switch

apis.description: API implementations the build registers: one entry from the top-level "apiSets" map. A trimmed build ships no client for the APIs it drops, so models.json can only name the APIs its set carries. Flavors set it as a name, not a switch

module/extra.description: Run-mode, permission, and webui bridge module (packages/extra, @nanopi/pi-extra); a flavor that drops it aliases the module to an inert stub

module/codex-compaction.description: Codex-style compaction and its post-compaction warning

module/qoder-checkin.description: Qoder daily check-in on session start (claims the campaign credits for every logged-in Qoder account)

module/pi-memory.description: Memory distillation: /remember, extracted in the background

module/websearch.description: web_search and read_page tools with the keyless engine chain

sidecar/tui-native.description: TUI native prebuilds builtin in single-file builds (all platforms embedded; the matching one installs to the agent bin directory, otherwise downloaded on demand). `full` leaves this off: the four prebuilds are the worst-compressing payload in the bundle (4.19 MiB raw, 0.90 MiB packed) and the download path is the same one an embedded-but-missing platform already takes

sidecar/photon-wasm.description: photon wasm builtin in single-file builds (installed to the agent bin directory, otherwise downloaded on demand). `full` leaves this off for the same reason as `sidecar/tui-native`: the download fallback is the original design, and the wasm is only needed once an image or the clipboard is touched

oauth/qoder-oauth.description: Qoder OAuth login flow (qoder.com and qoder.com.cn)

full.description: Everything included except the embedded native sidecars, which download on demand; the only flavor the npm packages are published from

base.description: Core CLI with the standard tool set (read, edit, write, bash), a curated model catalog (openai, google, anthropic, glm/z.ai, qwen, kimi, openrouter, opencode), every endpoint API implementation, and the export to Markdown and HTML; none of the bundled extras, docs, examples, the browser UI, sidecars or OAuth flows, so a login that needs a flow has to use an API key. Bedrock is not in this SKU: its implementations are dropped with the AWS SDK they pull (see `apiSets.endpoint`), so a `models.json` entry naming a bedrock api is skipped. Any other vendor is one `models.json` entry away

minimal.description: base with the bash tool alone, one endpoint shape, and no peripheral code: the shell tool is the only tool the build registers (the other tool definitions are stubbed out), endpoint API implementations are cut to openai-completions, the syntax-highlight grammars and embedded-code detection are dropped, every export format falls away, run modes and permissions (module/extra) fall away with the extras, and the endpoint and key come from models.json instead of a shipped catalog

all.description: Every API implementation in packages/ai. The marker is checked against the registered API ids at build time, and the runtime registers everything it ships

openai.description: The OpenAI-compatible chat completions API alone: the smallest build talks to one endpoint shape, which is everything models.json needs to point at a local or self-hosted server

endpoint.description: Every endpoint implementation except the cloud-vendor ones: the AWS Bedrock APIs (bedrock-converse-stream, bedrock-mantle-*) and the two shapes nothing in a trimmed build registers (cloudflare-workers-ai-system-one, openai-decisions) are dropped. A build on this set carries no AWS SDK and no `@aws/bedrock-token-generator` client, so `models.json` cannot name a bedrock api: an entry that does is skipped at load time (packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts). Measured on the base artifact: 870 KiB, 428 KiB of it the Bedrock implementations and the rest a second copy of @smithy that only the AWS variant of the openai client pulls

all.description: Every built-in provider catalog in packages/ai. A curated list, not everything models.dev lists: a catalog is kept when someone can plausibly type its key on purpose — the assistants people reach for first (openai, anthropic, google, glm/z.ai, kimi, qwen, xai, meta, deepseek, moonshot), the subscription plans (github-copilot, openrouter, vercel-ai-gateway, ollama-cloud, the token plans), and the hosts a large account brings (amazon-bedrock, azure, google-vertex). The rest of models.dev — the aggregators nobody has heard of, the hosts that resize a catalog of someone else's models, and the vendors with one or two models — is a `models.json` entry away and ships no data. `full` and `presets` ship this set; the model generator writes the concrete list back here, so a build never ships a provider the catalog does not have

core.description: The vendors a trimmed CLI keeps in its model picker: the assistants people reach for first (openai, google, anthropic, glm/z.ai, qwen, kimi) plus the two subscription aggregators with a real install base (openrouter, opencode + opencode-go) and amazon-bedrock, the one host whose credentials a server-side CLI already has through the environment (`bedrockAuth.resolve` reads AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, AWS_PROFILE and the AWS credential chain, so `base` can use it without an OAuth flow). Every other catalog stays a one-entry `models.json` away but ships no data, which is where the rest of the bundle's model data goes. `base` ships this set; `full` ships `all`

none.description: No built-in provider at all: the model generator writes an empty catalog, the runtime registers no built-in provider, and the endpoint and key come from models.json. This is the minimal SKU, which is why the set is a value and not a switch

presets.description: The preset providers a standard deployment configures: one catalog per vendor the CLI can talk to out of the box. Every member needs a reason to be here — a hand-written integration, an OAuth flow, or a subscription plan people pay for — because the data is the cost and a catalog nobody recognizes is worse than a `models.json` entry. The full set has the same members today; the two part ways as soon as the catalog grows an internal or stand-in provider
